reference_sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(t.n_promotions), 2) AS avg_promotions
FROM (
  -- one row per product in a promotion
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_promotions
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY product_id
) AS t
alternatives:
WITH product_promotions AS (
  -- one row per product in a promotion
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_promotions
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n_promotions), 2) AS avg_promotions
FROM product_promotions

SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT product_id), 2) AS avg_promotions
FROM promotion_products

other_way.sql:
SELECT ROUND(COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT product_id), 2) AS avg_promotions
FROM promotion_products
other_way.tradeoff: Dividing the pairs by the distinct products needs no inner step, but hides the one-row-per-product grain the average works on.
